mainTopic: בל תאחר: the five opinions on how many רגלים must pass and their sources, and the תשלומין of שבועות
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about בל תאחר, the Torah's command not to delay what you owe, including the poor-gifts of לקט, שכחה and פאה. The ברייתא gives five opinions on when the violation happens. The תנא קמא says after three רגלים, and רבי שמעון says three in order, ending with סוכות. רבי מאיר says one רגל, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says two, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says once סוכות passes. The גמרא then gives each opinion's verse and explains how the other side reads that verse differently. Next it asks what רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learn from the list of three festivals. They use it to teach that שבועות is compared to פסח, so שבועות has seven days of תשלומין. The גמרא asks why we don't compare שבועות to סוכות and give it eight days. It concludes with the rule תפשת מרובה לא תפשת: when in doubt, take the smaller number. Finally it asks why the verse mentions סוכות, and begins to answer that it compares סוכות to פסח. That answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Gifts to the poor also fall under the three-Festival rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא (whose earlier lines listed vows and pledges) adds that לקט, שכחה and פאה also violate בל תאחר once three רגלים pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field: once three Festivals have passed over them, one transgresses 'You shall not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא that lists the obligations covered by בל תאחר. Here it adds the three agricultural gifts to the poor and gives the opinion of the תנא קמא: the violation happens after three רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תאחר is not only about vows to the Temple. Gifts owed to the poor are also obligations, so delaying them is also a violation. This is the opinion of the anonymous first תנא, and the following opinions will argue with his count of 'three'.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest and belong to the poor
Forgotten sheaves left in the field, which belong to the poor
The corner of the field left unharvested for the poor
The three pilgrimage Festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
The prohibition 'You shall not delay' in paying what you owe

phrases.english: Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field,
phrases.notes: Continuing the list from earlier in the ברייתא

phrases.english: once three Festivals have passed over them —
he transgresses 'You shall not delay.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of obligations on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, delaying לקט, שכחה and פאה (like the other obligations) violates בל תאחר after three רגלים pass.

steps.title: רבי שמעון requires the three Festivals in order
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון agrees about three רגלים but requires them in their proper order, starting with פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: three Festivals in their order, with חג המצות first.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a condition to the three-רגלים rule. It is not just any three Festivals. They must go פסח, then שבועות, then סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose someone made a vow just before שבועות. For the תנא קמא, שבועות, סוכות and פסח would complete the three. For רבי שמעון, he must wait until the next סוכות, because the cycle has to start with פסח and end with סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The Festival of מצות, i.e., פסח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not counting more Festivals. He still counts three, but he requires a specific sequence, which can make the wait longer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
three Festivals in their order,
and the Festival of Matzos first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the תנא קמא's three-רגלים rule with a requirement of order
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One violates בל תאחר only after three רגלים pass in sequence: פסח, שבועות, סוכות.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: one Festival is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that one violates בל תאחר after just a single רגל passes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: once one Festival has passed over them, one transgresses 'You shall not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a much stricter opinion. One Festival going by is already too long a delay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a major disagreement with the תנא קמא. The question is no longer which three Festivals count. It is how many need to pass at all. For רבי מאיר, the first רגל is the deadline.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
once one Festival has passed over them —
he transgresses 'You shall not delay.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the number of רגלים set by the תנא קמא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One violates בל תאחר after a single רגל passes.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: two Festivals
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that the violation occurs after two רגלים pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: once two Festivals have passed over them, one transgresses 'You shall not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא gives a middle position. Two Festivals must pass, not one and not three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have a range of opinions: one רגל (רבי מאיר), two (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), and three (תנא קמא and רבי שמעון). Each opinion presumably reads the Torah's verses differently, and the גמרא begins explaining them right after the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
once two Festivals have passed over them —
he transgresses 'You shall not delay.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a middle position between רבי מאיר and the תנא קמא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One violates בל תאחר after two רגלים pass.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: once סוכות passes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that the violation is tied to סוכות passing, whatever the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: once חג הסוכות has passed over them, one transgresses 'You shall not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The last opinion in the ברייתא ties the deadline to a specific Festival, סוכות, instead of to a number of Festivals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, what matters is reaching the end of the Festival year, which is סוכות. Even if only one רגל has passed, once that רגל is סוכות the person has violated. This ends the ברייתא's list of opinions.
steps.whatToRemember: Five opinions on בל תאחר: תנא קמא says three רגלים; רבי שמעון says three in order, from פסח to סוכות; רבי מאיר says one; רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says two; רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says once סוכות passes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
once the Festival of Sukkos has passed over them —
he transgresses regarding them 'You shall not delay.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a fifth view based on a specific Festival rather than a count
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One violates בל תאחר once סוכות passes.

steps.title: What is the source of the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the תנא קמא's requirement of three רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finished, and the גמרא now starts explaining each opinion. This line sets up the next step, where the source for the תנא קמא will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a request for the Torah source behind the three-רגלים rule. The answer will come from a seemingly extra phrase in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, anonymous opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first Tanna? —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of opinions to explaining their sources
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for requiring three רגלים before violating בל תאחר

steps.title: The repeated names of the Festivals teach the three-Festival rule
steps.stepSummary: The Torah lists פסח, שבועות and סוכות again even though the section just discussed them. That extra listing teaches that בל תאחר applies after all three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the passage has just finished discussing them, why do I need the Torah to go back and write 'בחג המצות ובחג השבועות ובחג הסוכות'? Learn from it that it is for 'You shall not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. דברים טז has just finished describing all the Festivals, so naming all three again in פסוק טז seems unnecessary. The extra words must be teaching something new: the three-רגלים rule of בל תאחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a classic 'extra words' derivation. The Torah does not repeat itself for no reason, so a seemingly unneeded repetition is read as a new lesson. Here, listing all three רגלים together teaches that the deadline for paying obligations is after all three have passed.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all (introduces an obvious premise)
To go back and write again

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'למה לי' is not an attack on the תנא קמא. It is part of his proof: the repetition looks unnecessary, so it must be teaching something.

phrases.english: Since it has just finished with them,
phrases.notes: The section in דברים טז just discussed the Festivals

phrases.english: why do I need it to go back and write:
'On the Festival of Matzos, and on the Festival of Shavuos, and on the Festival of Sukkos'?
Learn from it: it is for 'You shall not delay.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ סָלֵיק לְמָה לִי לְמֶהְדַּר וּמִיכְתַּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the תנא קמא's source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seemingly redundant listing of all three רגלים in דברים טז:טז teaches that בל תאחר applies once all three have passed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the count of 'three' comes from reading extra words in a פסוק. The other opinions will need their own readings of the same section.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's source: סוכות must come last
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points out that repeating סוכות is extra, since the Torah was just speaking about it. That extra mention teaches that סוכות must be the last of the three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון says: it did not need to say 'בחג הסוכות,' since the verse was just speaking about it. Why was it stated? To say that this one is last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי שמעון's source for requiring the רגלים in order. The mention of סוכות in the list is especially extra, so it teaches that the cycle must end with סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים just before (דברים טז:יג-טו) discuss סוכות, so naming it yet again is doubly unnecessary. רבי שמעון reads this as a signal that סוכות closes the cycle. That means the three רגלים must run פסח, שבועות, סוכות in order.

keyTerms.meaning: It did not need to say
Which the verse was already speaking about

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: the extra listing of all three רגלים teaches three Festivals. רבי שמעון: the extra mention of סוכות teaches that סוכות must be last, so the Festivals must go in order.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon says:
it did not need to say 'on the Festival of Sukkos,'
since the verse was speaking about it,
phrases.notes: The preceding פסוקים deal with סוכות

phrases.english: why was it stated? —
to say that this one is last.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תנא קמא's source to רבי שמעון's source, building on the same פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra mention of סוכות, right after the Torah discussed it, teaches that סוכות must be the final רגל, so the three must be in order.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי מאיר's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's view that בל תאחר is violated after just one רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר holds that one violates בל תאחר after only one רגל. This sets up the next step, which brings his verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא already explained the תנא קמא's source for three רגלים. Now it turns to the opinion with the shortest deadline. One רגל needs its own source, because the three-רגלים verse does not support it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asks for the source or logic)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר holds that one is in violation after a single Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תנא קמא's source to רבי מאיר's source, following the same pattern as step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for violating בל תאחר after one רגל.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's verse: 'There you shall come, and there you shall bring'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns from the verse that pairs coming to the מקדש with bringing offerings. When you come on the first רגל, you must bring them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you shall come there… and you shall bring there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse. The verse links 'coming there' (going up on a רגל) with 'bringing there' (bringing your offerings).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two phrases sit side by side, the first time you go up, you are supposed to bring what you owe. So once a single רגל passes without the offering, you are already late.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall come there (to the מקדש)
And you shall bring there (your offerings)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you shall come there…'
phrases.notes: דברים יב:ה: going up to the מקדש.

phrases.english: '…and you shall bring there.'
phrases.notes: דברים יב:ו: bringing the vows and offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse ties bringing offerings to the first time one comes to the מקדש, which is the first רגל.

steps.title: The רבנן: that verse is only a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that the verse 'there you shall bring' teaches a מצות עשה to bring offerings on the first רגל. Missing it does not violate בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? That verse teaches a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with רבי מאיר's verse. It answers that, in their view, the verse only creates a מצות עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree you should bring offerings on the first רגל. But if you don't, you only miss a positive מצוה. The לאו of בל תאחר still needs three רגלים to pass.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (here, the תנא קמא who require three רגלים)

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not saying there is no obligation at the first רגל. There is a real מצות עשה then. They only say the לאו of בל תאחר does not start yet.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? That verse is for a positive commandment.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is really asking here: what do the רבנן do with this פסוק?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the רבנן read רבי מאיר's verse differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the verse: an עשה, not a trigger for the לאו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse seems to prove that the first רגל is the deadline for בל תאחר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse only sets a מצות עשה for the first רגל. בל תאחר comes later.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: missing the Torah's time automatically means delaying
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that once the Torah commands you to bring the offering at a certain time and you don't, you have automatically violated בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? Since the Merciful One told him 'bring,' and he did not bring, he automatically stands in violation of 'do not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי מאיר's reply to the רבנן. He says the עשה and the לאו cannot be separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן tried to limit the verse to a מצות עשה. רבי מאיר argues that the Torah's command sets the deadline. Missing that deadline is exactly what 'delaying' means, so בל תאחר applies right away.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, i.e., the Torah
The prohibition against delaying a vow

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the Torah's command to bring at the first רגל sets the deadline, so missing it violates בל תאחר. רבנן: the first רגל is only a מצות עשה, and בל תאחר needs three רגלים.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir: since the Merciful One told him
phrases.notes: The גמרא is really asking here: how does רבי מאיר answer that?

phrases.english: 'Bring!' and he did not bring,
automatically he stands in violation of 'You shall not delay.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא אַיְיתִי וְלָא אַיְיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבנן's attempt in step 11 to limit the verse to an עשה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The רבנן's claim that the verse creates only an עשה with no link to בל תאחר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Once the Torah sets a time, failing to act by then is itself delaying, so the עשה and the לאו go together.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that בל תאחר is violated after two רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of the middle opinion: two רגלים. This sets up the verse in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 gave his view without a source. Two needs its own explanation, because it fits neither the three-רגלים verse nor רבי מאיר's one-רגל verse.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, מַאי טַעְמָא?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר's source to the next opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for violating בל תאחר after two רגלים.

steps.title: 'In your appointed times': a plural means at least two
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns from 'במועדיכם' (in your appointed times). The word is plural, and the smallest plural is two, so the deadline is two רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'These you shall do to ה׳ in your appointed times.' The minimum of 'appointed times' is two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse that connects bringing vows to the 'מועדים.' Since the word is plural, it means at least two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says vows belong to 'your appointed times' in the plural. We assume the plural means the smallest possible number, which is two. So once two רגלים pass, the time has run out.
steps.whatToRemember: Each opinion has its own source: the תנא קמא learns three from the extra listing of the רגלים, רבי מאיר learns one from 'there you shall come… there you shall bring,' and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns two from the plural 'במועדיכם.'

phrases.english: As it is written: 'These you shall do to the Lord in your appointed times,'
phrases.notes: במדבר כט:לט, which continues 'besides your vows and your gift offerings.'

phrases.english: the minimum of 'appointed times' is two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural 'מועדיכם' means at least two רגלים, so בל תאחר applies after two.

steps.title: The רבנן use 'במועדיכם' for רבי יונה's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן don't learn the two-רגלים rule from 'במועדיכם'. They use the word for רבי יונה's teaching that all the festivals are compared to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They use that word for the teaching of רבי יונה. רבי יונה said: All the festivals are compared to one another, because all their offerings atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the רבנן do with the word 'במועדיכם', which רבי אליעזר בן יעקב just used for the two-רגלים rule. The רבנן say the word teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא follows a rule: if one תנא learns something from a word, the other side must explain what that word teaches them. For the רבנן, 'במועדיכם' teaches that all the festivals are linked. Because of that link, the goat offerings of every festival atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared (linked by a היקש, so the same law applies to all)
Entering the Temple or eating holy food while impure, without knowing it

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: This is a short way of asking: what do the רבנן do with 'במועדיכם'?

phrases.english: That word is needed for the teaching of Rabbi Yona.
For Rabbi Yona said:

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְשׁוּ כׇּל הַמּוֹעֲדִים כּוּלָּם זֶה לָזֶה,
phrases.english: All the festivals are compared to one another,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכּוּלָּן מְכַפְּרִים עַל טוּמְאַת מִקְדָּשׁ וְקָדָשָׁיו.
phrases.english: that all of them atone for impurity of the Temple and its holy foods.
phrases.notes: This refers to the goat offerings of the festivals, which are like the goat of ראש חודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the other side reads the verse that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב used in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an answer, it would seem the רבנן have no use for 'במועדיכם', which would suggest they must agree with the two-רגלים rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן use 'במועדיכם' for רבי יונה's teaching that all the festivals are linked.

steps.title: What is רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view. He holds that once סוכות passes, you have violated בל תאחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last opinion in the list and asks where it comes from. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that סוכות is the deadline. It doesn't matter how many רגלים have passed, and it doesn't matter when the vow was made. The גמרא wants to know which verse he learns this from.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next תנא in the list of opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view that the end of סוכות is the deadline.

steps.title: The extra mention of סוכות shows that סוכות is the deadline
steps.stepSummary: The Torah was already talking about סוכות, so it did not need to name 'חג הסוכות' again. The extra mention teaches that סוכות is what makes you late.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: The verse did not need to say 'חג הסוכות', because the verses right before were already about it. So why does it say it? To teach that this festival is what causes the violation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The verse names סוכות even though it didn't need to, and that extra mention is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in דברים ט״ז:ט״ז comes right after the section about סוכות. Repeating the name looks unnecessary, so it must be teaching something. It teaches that סוכות itself is the deadline: by the end of סוכות, every vow must already be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: It didn't need to be said
Since the verse was already talking about it

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
The verse did not need to say 'the festival of Sukkot',
since the verses before were already speaking about it.
Why then is it said?
To say that this festival is what causes the violation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An extra word in the verse: 'חג הסוכות' is repeated, which teaches that סוכות is the deadline.

steps.title: What do רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learn from the list of three festivals?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן used 'בחג המצות ובחג השבועות ובחג הסוכות' for the three-רגלים rule. So what do רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: what do they learn from the verse 'בחג המצות ובחג השבועות ובחג הסוכות'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what this verse teaches the two תנאים who don't need three רגלים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says one רגל and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says two. Neither of them uses the list of three festivals for בל תאחר. So the גמרא asks what that verse teaches them.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they learn from it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת וּבְחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת״
phrases.english: this verse, 'On the festival of Matzos, and on the festival of Shavuos, and on the festival of Sukkos',
what do they learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב: הַאי ״בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת וּבְחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת״ מַאי דָּרְשׁוּ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other opinions use the verse the רבנן used for three רגלים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learn from the list of three festivals.

steps.title: The verse teaches that שבועות has seven days to make up its offering
steps.stepSummary: They use the verse for רבי אלעזר's teaching in the name of רבי אושעיא. שבועות is compared to פסח, so שבועות also has seven days of תשלומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for the teaching of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא: How do we know that עצרת (שבועות) has seven days of תשלומין? The verse says 'בחג המצות ובחג השבועות ובחג הסוכות.' It compares שבועות to פסח. Just as פסח has seven days of תשלומין, so too שבועות has seven days of תשלומין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse teaches a different law. A person who did not bring his festival offering on the day of שבועות may still bring it during the next six days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח and שבועות are named side by side, so the Torah is comparing them. פסח lasts seven days, so its offering can be brought on any of those days. שבועות is only one day, but because of this comparison it also gets seven days to bring the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it (for a different teaching)
Make-up days for bringing a festival offering that was missed

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'עצרת' means שבועות, not שמיני עצרת. Also, these are make-up days for the festival offering. This is not about בל תאחר.

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְכִדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא.
phrases.english: They need it for the teaching of Rabbi Elazar, who said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִין לַעֲצֶרֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כׇּל שִׁבְעָה?
phrases.english: From where do we know that Shavuos has make-up days for all seven days?
The verse teaches:
'On the festival of Matzos, and on the festival of Shavuos, and on the festival of Sukkos.'
It compares the festival of Shavuos to the festival of Matzos:

phrases.aramaic: מָה חַג הַמַּצּוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כׇּל שִׁבְעָה —
phrases.english: just as the festival of Matzos has make-up days for all seven days,

phrases.aramaic: אַף חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ תַּשְׁלוּמִין כׇּל שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: so too the festival of Shavuos has make-up days for all seven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְכִדְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by giving the verse a different use.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse compares שבועות to פסח, which teaches seven days of תשלומין for שבועות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source in the גמרא for the halacha that the offerings of שבועות can be brought for seven days.

steps.title: Why not compare שבועות to סוכות and give it eight days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the comparison. סוכות is also in the verse, so why not compare שבועות to סוכות and give it eight days?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us compare it to סוכות instead: just as there it is eight days, so too here it should be eight days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the comparison just made. שבועות sits between פסח and סוכות in the verse, so it could just as easily be compared to סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse links the festivals, why pick פסח as the model and not סוכות? Counting שמיני עצרת, סוכות seems to have eight days. That would give שבועות eight days of תשלומין.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it be compared to

phrases.english: Then let it be compared to the festival of Sukkos:
just as there it is eight days,
so too here it should be eight days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison made in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שבועות gets exactly seven days of תשלומין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סוכות also appears next to שבועות in the verse and seems to have eight days, so why not give שבועות eight?

steps.title: The eighth day is a separate festival
steps.stepSummary: שמיני עצרת is its own רגל, not part of סוכות. So סוכות also has only seven days, and the comparison gives seven either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The eighth day is a separate festival on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Comparing שבועות to סוכות would also give seven days, because the eighth day does not belong to סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that סוכות lasts eight days. But שמיני עצרת is a separate festival with its own identity. So the festival offering of סוכות can only be made up during the seven days of סוכות, and both comparisons lead to seven days.
steps.whatToRemember: This answer says סוכות has only seven days because שמיני עצרת is a separate רגל. The next step challenges this answer, and the final reason שבועות gets seven days comes in step 24 (תפשת מרובה לא תפשת).

phrases.english: The eighth day is a festival in its own right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting a wrong assumption about the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סוכות lasts eight days, so comparing to it would give שבועות eight days of תשלומין.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמיני עצרת is a separate רגל, so סוכות has only seven days and the comparison still gives seven.

steps.title: For make-up offerings, the eighth day still belongs to סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 21. שמיני עצרת is its own רגל only for six things (פז"ר קש"ב). For תשלומין, everyone agrees it is a make-up day for the first day of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could say: we only call שמיני עצרת a separate festival for the six things of פז"ר קש"ב. For make-up offerings, everyone agrees it is a make-up day for the first day of סוכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 21. It says that answer only works for some laws, not for תשלומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said סוכות has only seven days because שמיני עצרת is its own רגל. Here the גמרא says that is true only for six specific laws. For bringing a late offering, שמיני עצרת still counts as part of סוכות. So סוכות has eight days of תשלומין, and the question returns: why not compare שבועות to סוכות and give it eight?

keyTerms.meaning: Say / perhaps say. Opens a possible objection.
The eighth day, right after the seven days of סוכות
A festival in its own right, separate from סוכות
Memory code for six ways שמיני עצרת is separate: פַּיִס (lottery), זְמַן (שהחיינו), רֶגֶל (its own festival), קָרְבָּן (its own offering), שִׁיר (its own song), בְּרָכָה (its own blessing)
Make-up days. Extra days to bring a festival offering you missed on the first day.

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'its own רגל' is not all-or-nothing. שמיני עצרת is separate for some laws (פז"ר קש"ב) but still connected to סוכות for תשלומין.

phrases.english: But say that when we say
that the Eighth Day is a festival on its own
it is only regarding the six things of פז"ר קש"ב
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for one thing: lottery, the blessing on time, festival, offering, song, and blessing.

phrases.english: but regarding make-up offerings
everyone agrees
it is a make-up day for the first day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמְרִינַן שְׁמִינִי רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 21 by limiting where שמיני עצרת counts as separate.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 21 that סוכות has only seven days of תשלומין because שמיני עצרת is its own רגל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The separateness of שמיני עצרת covers only פז"ר קש"ב. For תשלומין it is part of סוכות, so סוכות has eight days and the Step 20 question returns.

steps.title: A משנה shows the last day counts as a make-up day
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if someone did not bring his חגיגה on the first day of סוכות, he can bring it all the festival, including the last day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if someone did not bring his festival offering on the first day of סוכות, he may bring it all through the festival, and even on the last day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove the challenge in Step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'last day' in this משנה is שמיני עצרת. So for bringing a late חגיגה, שמיני עצרת counts as part of סוכות. That gives סוכות eight days of תשלומין.

keyTerms.meaning: The last festival day of סוכות, meaning שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: As we learned: one who did not bring the festival offering
on the first festival day of סוכות
may bring it all through the festival
and on the last festival day of סוכות.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source that supports the challenge of Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That שמיני עצרת is a day of תשלומין for סוכות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (חגיגה) saying a missed חגיגה may be brought through the last day of the festival.

steps.title: When in doubt, take the smaller number
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a rule: if you grab a lot, you may end up with nothing; if you grab a little, you keep it. So we compare שבועות to פסח (seven days), not to סוכות (eight).
steps.simpleTranslation: If you grabbed a lot, you did not grab anything. If you grabbed a little, you got it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Since שבועות could be compared to either פסח or סוכות, we choose the smaller number of days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven days is included inside eight, so seven is certain. Eight might be too much. So when the comparison could give seven or eight, we go with seven, and שבועות gets seven days of תשלומין.
steps.whatToRemember: תפשת מרובה לא תפשת: when unsure between two amounts, take the smaller one, because it is surely included in the larger.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule used across ש"ס whenever a comparison could give two different amounts.

phrases.english: If you grabbed a lot, you did not grab anything;
if you grabbed a little, you got it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 22-23 without denying that סוכות has eight days.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general rule for choosing between two possible comparisons.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since סוכות has eight days of תשלומין, maybe שבועות should get eight days too.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the comparison could give seven or eight, we take the smaller sure amount, seven, as with פסח.

steps.title: Then why does the verse mention סוכות?
steps.stepSummary: If שבועות is compared only to פסח, the גמרא asks what law we learn from the verse naming חג הסוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, for what law did the Torah write 'חג הסוכות' in this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the comparison to סוכות is not used for שבועות, the גמרא asks why the verse names סוכות at all. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the Torah should teach something. If סוכות is not used for the שבועות comparison, its mention seems extra. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (the Merciful One) wrote it

phrases.english: But then for what law
did the Torah write 'the festival of סוכות'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא כַּתְבֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא לְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 24: once סוכות is not used for שבועות, its mention needs a reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law is learned from the mention of חג הסוכות in the verse?

steps.title: To compare סוכות to פסח
steps.stepSummary: The mention of סוכות is there to compare סוכות to פסח. The details continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: To compare it to the festival of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that סוכות is named in order to link it to פסח. It is setting up the explanation of what that link teaches, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison here goes the other way: not שבועות to סוכות, but סוכות to פסח. Some law of פסח will be applied to סוכות, and the גמרא will spell it out next.

keyTerms.meaning: To compare it (a היקש, a link between two things in one verse)

phrases.english: To compare it to the festival of מצות (פסח):

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse names סוכות to create a היקש between סוכות and פסח. The specific law follows in the next lines.
